minutes.headline: Select Board backed the fire department's move to the advanced EMT license level and ratified three reserve police officers.
minutes.summary: The board transferred a package store liquor license, ratified three reserve police officers, and heard the fire chief explain the state's change to the advanced EMT level, which it supported. It reviewed three draft personnel policies and put them over to next week. Committee reports covered the school building and building reuse property line question, and the town manager gave a state Senate budget update before a joint executive session on a litigation matter.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to support the fire department's move to the advanced EMT license level, after the fire chief explained the state's change.
The board transferred the all-alcoholic package store license at Lunenburg Liquors to SAR Judas LLC.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of three reserve police officers.
Three draft personnel policies (harassment, social media, professional conduct) were put over to next week, with the town manager to check coverage of officials and volunteers.
The town manager said the Senate budget version adds Chapter 70 school aid for Lunenburg, not yet approved, and cuts kindergarten grants compared to the House.

why_it_matters: The advanced EMT change carries equipment, training and medication costs, to be absorbed over two years from the budget and donation funds, plus personnel costs subject to bargaining, which can reach the town budget, mostly taxes.
The Senate and House budget versions differ on school aid and kindergarten grants, so the state aid available to the schools is not yet settled.
watch_next: The three draft personnel policies return to the board's agenda next week.
Board liaisons for the Conservation Commission and ZBA are to be raised next week; members are to meet the town manager on her evaluation by end of May, for presentation in early June.
